investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. The scheduler message (evidence id: failed-check.message) reports two distinct blocking conditions: (1) the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource have zero remaining allocatable VM slots — "2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" — and (2) the other 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector constraints — "4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector". Preemption was also exhausted: no lower-priority victims were found on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained unscheduled for ~148 seconds before the eval timed out, producing an empty evidence object and failing all four required-evidence assertions. This is an eval-detected infrastructure scheduling constraint failure scoped to the remote-agents feature in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all allocatable VM slots are consumed by existing workloads or leaked/stuck pods, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. Supported by the explicit 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message in all three sibling check failures (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

SECONDARY — node affinity or node selector misconfiguration: the pod's affinity/selector rules restrict scheduling to a subset of nodes that either no longer exists or has been relabeled, reducing the eligible pool to only the 2 kata-capable nodes which are themselves exhausted. Supported by '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' in failed-check.message.

TERTIARY — leaked or zombie remote-agent pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: previously created remote-agent pods that were not cleaned up may be occupying all VM slots on the 2 eligible nodes, preventing new allocations. Consistent with the eval's use of withCleanup (source-context run-status-probes.mjs:1883) which implies cleanup is expected but may not have completed in a prior run.

LOWER CONFIDENCE — cluster under-provisioning: the cluster may have been scaled down or nodes removed, reducing the total kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity below the demand level. No node count change evidence is present in the packet; this remains a hypothesis.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. The scheduler message (evidence id: failed-check.message) reports two distinct blocking conditions: (1) the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource have zero remaining allocatable VM slots — "2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" — and (2) the other 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector constraints — "4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector". Preemption was also exhausted: no lower-priority victims were found on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained unscheduled for ~148 seconds before the eval timed out, producing an empty evidence object and failing all four required-evidence assertions. This is an eval-detected infrastructure scheduling constraint failure scoped to the remote-agents feature in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required peer-pod VM onto any of the 6 available nodes — 2 nodes reported insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. The eval probe timed out waiting for the pod to become schedulable, so no agent was ever created and the expected-output contract received zero evidence fields.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that are eligible by node affinity/selector. With 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod creation attempt is immediately Unschedulable. Because no pod ever starts, the eval runner's createAgent call never returns a live agent, and the check terminates with an empty evidence object — violating all 5 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) defined in the expected-output contract. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes: the extended resource quota for peer-pod VMs is fully consumed, leaving no schedulable capacity for new remote-agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message across all three failing checks.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: only 2 of 6 nodes are eligible for remote-agent pods by affinity/selector rules; if those 2 nodes are saturated there is no fallback, making the cluster effectively zero-capacity for this workload.

Tertiary — no preemption victims available: the scheduler message confirms preemption was attempted and found no lower-priority pods to evict on the 2 eligible nodes, ruling out a transient scheduling race and indicating sustained saturation.

Lower confidence — a recent cluster scaling event or node failure may have reduced the number of eligible nodes or the per-node kata.peerpods.io/vm quota below the level needed to run eval probes concurrently with production workloads; no node-event or scaling evidence is present in the packet to confirm or deny this.
